Comprehensive Data Quality Analysis

Source: R/na.R
check_na.Rd

Analyze missing values and special values (e.g. "unknown", "blank", "n/a") for each variable. Returns a styled gt table with conditional formatting based on severity.

Usage

check_na(data, ..., pattern = NULL, special = NULL, show_all = FALSE)

Arguments

data

A data.frame with unique, non-empty column names. Selected columns must be one-dimensional. Grouped inputs are inspected across all rows.

...

Variable selection using dplyr::select syntax. Omit to inspect all columns. Renaming changes only the displayed variable names.

pattern

NULL or a single non-missing character string used as a regex pattern for matching variable names. Takes precedence over ..., with a warning when both are supplied; an invalid regular expression is an error. An empty string matches all columns. An unmatched pattern or selection inspects no columns and returns NULL with an informational message.

special

NULL (default) for the built-in special-value markers, or a character vector of regular expressions that replaces them. Patterns are matched case-insensitively, with a Unicode-aware \b, anywhere in each whitespace-normalized value; anchor them with ^...$ or \b as needed. character(0) counts no special values, and empty strings count only when a pattern matches them.

show_all

A single non-missing logical. If FALSE (default), only variables with issues are shown.

Value

A gt table, returned visibly so that it prints in the console, renders in R Markdown, Quarto and pkgdown, and can be saved with gt::gtsave(). NULL, invisibly, when no table is produced: no selected columns, no rows, or no issues with show_all = FALSE.

Details

Inputs with zero rows or zero columns return NULL invisibly with an informational message and no table. Special-value counts apply to character and factor columns. Matching is case-insensitive and runs after collapsing whitespace, including Unicode spaces. The built-in markers are the whole words unknown(s), blank(s), n/a, na, missing, unspecified, not available, not applicable, not stated, not reported and null, values made only of ?, - or . characters, and empty or whitespace-only strings. A marker anywhere in a value counts it, so a category such as "Unknown primary site" counts as special; supply special to change the markers. Each value is counted once. Values recognized by is.na(), including SPSS user-missing codes, count only as missing values. Inspection loads methods for serialized haven-labelled and integer64 columns before counting missing values. Integer64 columns require the optional bit64 package. Dataset-size calculations use double precision, and counts are formatted as whole numbers without a 32-bit integer limit. Severity colors use unrounded percentages. Missing-value shading is yellow above 0%, orange above 20% and red above 50%, and also tints the variable and type cells. Special-value shading deepens from light to dark blue above 0%, 10% and 30%. A source note under the table repeats these thresholds. Percentages are rounded only for display, to one decimal place in cells and two in the summary. Positive percentages below these display resolutions appear as <0.1% in cells and <0.01% in the summary; zeros retain their usual numeric format. The subtitle counts variables containing issues; the summary counts individual missing and special values across the selected columns. Both summary percentages use every selected cell as the denominator, including columns that cannot hold special values.

See also

Other inspect: check_packages(), check_size(), check_system(), impute_na_knn(), lv(), plt_na()

Examples

# \donttest{
# Analyze all variables
check_na(airquality)
#>  check_na  2 variables with data quality issues
